In [[mathematics]], in the realm of [[group theory]], a [[Group (mathematics)|group]] is said to be '''critical''' if it is not in the [[variety (universal algebra)|variety]] generated by all its proper [[subquotient]]s, which includes all its [[subgroup]]s and all its [[quotient]]s.<ref name="Oates1964">{{cite journal |last1=Oates |first1=Sheila |last2=Powell |first2=M.B |title=Identical relations in finite groups |journal=Journal of Algebra |date=April 1964 |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=11–39 |doi=10.1016/0021-8693(64)90004-3 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0021869364900043?via%3Dihub |access-date=26 April 2024|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Definition ==

A factor of a group <math>G</math> is a group of the form <math>H/N</math>, where <math>H</math> is a [[subgroup]] of <math>G</math>, and <math>N</math> is a [[normal subgroup]] of <math>G</math>, and is called a proper factor when <math>N</math> is non-trivial or <math>H</math> is a proper subgroup. A group <math>G</math> is critical when it is [[finite group|finite]] as well as not within the [[Variety (universal algebra)|variety]] generated by the group's proper factors.<ref name="Cossey1969">{{cite journal |last1=Cossey |first1=John |title=Critical Groups and the Lattice of Varieties |journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |date=1969 |volume=20 |issue=1 |pages=217–221 |doi=10.2307/2035994 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2035994 |access-date=16 June 2025 |issn=0002-9939}}</ref> Critical groups were introduced by [[D. C. Cross]]<ref name="Kovács1966" />

=== Examples and non-examples ===

Every [[Finite simple group|finite simple group]] is critical.<ref name="Oates1964" /> On the other hand, if a group is generated by a subgroup with multiple normal subgroups of that group, but not generated from any proper subset of those normal subgroups with the subgroup, and if the commutator subgroup generated by the normal subgroups is trivial for every permutation involved in generating the commutator subgroup, then the group is not critical.<ref name="Oates1964" />

== Properties ==

Every critical group <math>G</math> has a unique minimal normal subgroup called the monolith, and this subgroup is denoted <math>\sigma G</math>.<ref name="Cossey1969" /> Such groups are called [[monolithic group|monolithic]], which are a necessary yet insufficient condition for being critical.<ref name="Neumann1967" />

* Any [[finite group|finite]] [[monolithic group|monolithic]] [[A-group]] is critical. This result is due to Kovacs and Newman.<ref name="Kovács1966">{{cite journal |last1=Kovács |first1=L. G. |last2=Newman |first2=M. F. |title=On critical groups |journal=Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society |date=May 1966 |volume=6 |issue=2 |pages=237–250 |doi=10.1017/S144678870000481X |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-australian-mathematical-society/article/on-critical-groups/9DC05B1E33B4896530FFDC8ED24CA395#}}</ref> But not every monolithic group is critical.<ref name="Neumann1967">{{cite book |last1=Neumann |first1=Hanna |title=Varieties of Groups |date=6 December 2012 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-642-88599-0 |page=147 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VaMjCQAAQBAJ |language=en}}</ref>
* The variety generated by a finite group has a finite number of nonisomorphic critical groups.<ref name="Oates1964" />

== Cross variety ==

A Cross variety is a [[Variety (universal algebra)|variety]] of groups that satisfies:<ref name="Oates1964" />
* The variety "has a finite basis for its identical relations"
* All [[finitely generated groups]] in the variety are necessarily finite.
* There are only a finite amount of critical groups in the variety.
[[Sheila Oates]] and [[M.B.Powell]] proved using Cross varieties that every finite group has a finite basis for the identical relations holding in the group.<ref name="Oates1964" /> They also proved that "[a] variety of groups is Cross if and only if it is generated by a finite group," which can be shown inductively from the fact that any variety generated by a Cross variety and a finite group is also a Cross variety.<ref name="Oates1964" />
